mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a convex lens from a concave lens?

options.A: A convex lens converges parallel rays to a real focus, whereas a concave lens diverges parallel rays as if they originated from a virtual focus.
options.B: A convex lens diverges parallel rays, while a concave lens converges them to a real focus.
options.C: Both convex and concave lenses converge parallel rays, but only convex lenses form virtual images.
options.D: Both convex and concave lenses diverge parallel rays, but only concave lenses can form real images.

mcqs.answer: A convex lens converges parallel rays to a real focus, whereas a concave lens diverges parallel rays as if they originated from a virtual focus.
mcqs.explanation: A convex (converging) lens brings parallel incident rays to a real focal point on the image side. A concave (diverging) lens spreads parallel rays so that they appear to come from a virtual focal point on the object side. The other options reverse these behaviours or state incorrect facts.

mcqs.question: The optical centre of a thin lens is the point through which:

options.A: All incident rays are reflected back towards the source.
options.B: Any incident ray passing through it continues in a straight line without deviation.
options.C: Only rays parallel to the principal axis are refracted.
options.D: All rays converge to the principal focus after passing through it.

mcqs.answer: Any incident ray passing through it continues in a straight line without deviation.
mcqs.explanation: The optical centre (also called the centre of the lens) is the point where the thickness of the lens is negligible, so a ray passing through it does not change direction. Reflections do not occur in a lens, and convergence to the focus happens after refraction, not at the centre.

mcqs.question: A convex lens of focal length 10 cm forms an image of a distant object at its principal focus. Where is the principal focus located relative to the lens?

options.A: 10 cm on the same side as the object (object side).
options.B: 10 cm on the opposite side of the lens (image side).
options.C: At the centre of the lens.

mcqs.answer: 10 cm on the opposite side of the lens (image side).
mcqs.explanation: For a convex lens, the principal (real) focus lies on the image side at a distance equal to the focal length. Since the focal length is 10 cm, the principal focus is 10 cm beyond the lens on the image side. The object side focus is virtual for a convex lens.

mcqs.question: A convex lens forms a real image of a candle placed 30 cm from the lens on a screen 60 cm on the other side. What is the focal length of the lens?
mcqs.explanation: Using the lens formula 1/f = 1/v – 1/u (sign convention: object distance u = –30 cm, image distance v = +60 cm), we get 1/f = 1/60 – (–1/30) = 1/60 + 1/30 = 3/60 = 1/20, so f = 20 cm. The other options result from incorrect arithmetic or misuse of the formula.

mcqs.question: When drawing a ray diagram for a convex lens, which of the following is a common mistake?

options.A: Assuming the ray passing through the optical centre deviates after the lens.
options.B: Drawing the ray parallel to the principal axis and passing through the focal point on the image side.
options.C: Using a ray that passes through the focal point on the object side and then emerges parallel to the principal axis.
options.D: Ensuring all three principal rays intersect at a single point to locate the image.

mcqs.answer: Assuming the ray passing through the optical centre deviates after the lens.
mcqs.explanation: The ray that passes through the optical centre of a thin lens does not change direction; assuming it deviates is a frequent misconception. Options B, C, and D describe correct steps in constructing ray diagrams.

mcqs.question: An object is placed 10 cm from a convex lens of focal length 5 cm (i.e., at 2F). What is the nature and position of the image formed?

options.A: Real, inverted, and formed at 2F on the opposite side of the lens.
options.B: Virtual, upright, and formed at 2F on the same side as the object.
options.C: Real, upright, and formed at the focal point on the opposite side.
options.D: Virtual, inverted, and formed at the focal point on the same side.

mcqs.answer: Real, inverted, and formed at 2F on the opposite side of the lens.
mcqs.explanation: For a convex lens, when the object is placed at twice the focal length (2F), the image is real, inverted, of the same size, and formed at 2F on the other side. The other options describe situations that occur with different object distances or with concave lenses.

mcqs.question: For an object placed beyond 2F, which pair correctly describes the image formed by a convex lens and a concave lens respectively?

options.A: Convex lens – real, inverted, reduced image between F and 2F; Concave lens – virtual, upright, reduced image between lens and focus.
options.B: Convex lens – virtual, upright, enlarged image beyond 2F; Concave lens – real, inverted, enlarged image beyond 2F.
options.C: Convex lens – real, upright, same size image at 2F; Concave lens – virtual, inverted image at the focal point.
options.D: Convex lens – virtual, upright, reduced image at the focal point; Concave lens – real, inverted, reduced image between F and 2F.

mcqs.answer: Convex lens – real, inverted, reduced image between F and 2F; Concave lens – virtual, upright, reduced image between lens and focus.
mcqs.explanation: When the object is beyond 2F, a convex lens forms a real, inverted, reduced image between the focal point (F) and 2F on the opposite side. A concave lens always forms a virtual, upright, reduced image on the same side as the object, located between the lens and its focal point. The other options mix up image nature, orientation, and location.

mcqs.question: In a competitive exam, a thin lens is said to have its optical centre at point O. Which statement about a ray passing through O is true?

options.A: The ray is reflected back towards the source.
options.B: The ray passes through the lens without any change in direction.
options.C: The ray bends towards the principal axis after passing through O.
options.D: The ray diverges as if it originated from the principal focus.

mcqs.answer: The ray passes through the lens without any change in direction.
mcqs.explanation: At the optical centre of a thin lens, the thickness is negligible, so a ray that passes through this point emerges undeviated. Reflection does not occur in lenses, and bending towards the axis or diverging from the focus happens only after refraction at other points, not at the centre.
